correctness.rationale: For any polynomial P the direct Jacobian has trace zero, vanishing determinant and vanishing sum of principal minors, proving pointwise nilpotence. An explicit polynomial automorphism conjugates N with G. For affine P, the real-scaled recurrence (r,s)->(s,(r-s)^2) leads for every fourth-period sequence to A=S(B-A), B=S(A+B), S=-2AB. The nonzero case forces S²=1/2 and (1+S)A²=-1/4, impossible over reals; the zero case forces all terms zero. Thus no nontrivial fourth-period point. For the quadratic example, the unique real algebraic t in (1,2) satisfies t²(t-1)=2 and four exact P-values, giving a four-state G orbit with distinct third coordinates. Standard-library exact quotient-ring checker reproduced all four transitions; calculation is confirmatory, not an infinite proof. No unstated assumptions or limits beyond the family.

originality.rationale: The published 2022 arXiv preprint poses an open question about analytical m-cycles for m>=4, while proving no 2-cycles, existence of 3-cycles, and a 5-cycle for affine P. Chamberland (2006) treats 2- and 3-cycles, and the apparent 4-cycle in his introduction belongs to a separate planar rational counterexample, not the nilpotent family. The new global affine exclusion and exact quadratic sharpness are not consequences of those inspected statements. Semantic searches of published research records and both historical ledgers did not reveal the same claim. Uninspected later journal details pose residual priority uncertainty; self-review originality is not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The 2022 source explicitly identifies analytical existence of cycles of least period m>=4 as open for this nilpotent-Jacobian dynamical family. The theorem settles one natural first missing period with the sharp defining-degree boundary (affine impossible, quadratic possible), combining a uniform structural obstruction and an exact realizability construction. This discriminates complexity of the system and clarifies why prior known 3- and affine 5-cycles do not determine period-four behavior. It is neither a routine substitution nor an arbitrary finite census; the limitations are stated, and no full all-period classification is claimed.
